page.layout: One text column, running full width down the page, with no margin notes printed. A handwritten annotation sits in the left margin and is not printed text. Show-through from the reverse side appears in the text block and is omitted.

main_text.l: tradi solent, una à vera Dei Ecclesia, Altera à

l.i: nam est integra conformitas motuum cordis,
& omnium virium cum Deo seu cum lege Dei. Idem
est enim dicere, congruere cum Deo, & congrue-
re cum lege Dei, quia Deus talis est, sicut se in lege descripsit.

main_text.l: Plato iusticiam uniuersalem sic definit, ut sit
iudicium rationis, id est, conseruatio ordinis
erga omnes leges honestas ad nos pertinentes, ut
Aristides nominatur iustus, quia non violat
ullam legem honestæ societatis, in qua versatur.

l.i: letters] μετὰ ἰσότητος, Iusticia est communicatio, qua Deus se nobis
iusticiam. Ac prior quidem pars loquitur de pri-
ma tabula, & de actionibus diuinis in renatis.

page.notes: The handwritten annotation "Axiomata theologica" in the left margin is manuscript, not printed, and is omitted. Ink strikethroughs cover "quia Deus talis est, sicut se" and "lege descripsit" in the first paragraph. The words are transcribed as printed. The strokes look like later manuscript cancellation. The Greek in the Clement quotation is only partly legible. The middle section is marked illegible and the opening and closing words are read from the scan with some doubt. The "K." and "K.I.", "K.II.", "K.III." markers and the "X." are printed section signs and are kept as paragraphs. No page number or running head is printed. "Etsi" at lower right is the catchword.
